verdicts.reason: Quote is line 6 of the blockquote word for word: "I don't think germline suits being in the waiting-on-design thing." The statement firms "I don't think X suits" into "do not belong", which Decided item 1's bold sentence (line 15) carries as a decision, so it does not overreach. 'germline' / 'germinal' is flagged in the note.

Quote is in the source across the line wrap at lines 6-7: "Germlines will just match in with animals" / "as a reference point for everything." Decided item 1 line 15-16 restates the same fact, so recording it once is right.
Quote is at lines 7-8 verbatim, including Sam's "If anything," hedge, which the note records honestly; the Decided list turns it into the decision, so the statement is supported rather than invented.

Quote "but that doesn't suit being separate." is at line 8. The referent of "that" is not spelled out in the quote, but the nearest noun phrase is the Germinals date calendar Sam has just said to fold in, and Decided item 1's merge into inc-053 reads it the same way, so the statement holds. Kind would sit as well under behaviour-free 'constraint', which is what it has.

Quote "Commodities search is being handled by a different ticket." is at line 8. The statement's added ", not by this work" follows from "a different ticket" and is said outright in Decided item 2's last sentence ("not to this backlog"), so it does not overreach.

Quote "Again, the call is blocked until it's been implemented." is at line 9. The statement names the call as the commodity-search design call and "it" as the different ticket; the blockquote leaves both pronouns unnamed, so strictly the confidence would be inferred rather than verbatim, but Decided item 2 (lines 19-20) reads them that way and the note already flags the ambiguity. Holds, with the confidence noted as loose.

Quote runs across lines 9-10 word for word: "Don't think you need something confirming a transit country has been added or removed when there's a row of transit countries added to a table." The statement restates it without the hedge, which Decided item 3's bold sentence makes a decision. The note's cross-references cannot be checked from this source, but distil/conflicts.json confirms c-006 carries the transit clause waiting on design question 4, so they are not invented.

Quote is at lines 10-11 verbatim. Rightly inferred: the source puts it as a rhetorical question, and the statement's reading (the table is itself the confirmation) is exactly what Decided item 3 line 22-23 records, so the inference is sound and the note says why it is inferred.

Quote is Decided item 1's bold sentence at line 15, asterisks included. Inferred is the right confidence: the blockquote never says "not a design question", and the note gives the two blockquote sentences it follows from.

Quote is at lines 16-17 across the wrap: "The germinal dates' 'Choose date' calendar (inc-192) leaves the" / "waiting-on-design theme". Inferred is right because the blockquote names no increment id. conflicts.json c-283 is indeed the germinal 'Choose date' calendar held on design question 12, so the note's reference stands.

Quote "is merged into the germinal identification dates row (inc-053)" is at line 17. The note is correct that the blockquote says only "one of the rows on Germinals" and does not name which, so naming inc-053 is the Decided list's reading, which the claim records rather than hides.

Quote is at lines 17-18 across the wrap, ending "as the interaction designer ruled on 9 November." The claim is careful: the blockquote is silent on the component, Decided item 1 cites another ruling as the authority, and the note tells the reconciler to take the component from ruling:interaction-designer-2026-11-09. Nothing overreaches.

Quote "The design call on results as you type (inc-014) stays blocked until that ticket has been implemented" is at lines 19-20 across the wrap. Inferred is right (no increment id in the blockquote), and conflicts.json c-012 is indeed commodity search as you type on design question 3, matching the note.

Quote "and does not go to the designer before then." is at line 20. Rightly inferred: the blockquote says only that the call is blocked, not who it is kept from, and the claim points at its own gap claim for how far "the designer" reaches.

Quote is Decided item 2's final sentence at lines 20-21 word for word. Splitting the joined sentence into this claim and -016 follows the one-fact rule, and inferred is right because the blockquote mentions no search button.

Same quote at lines 20-21, the 'cattle' half of the 'and'. Inferred is right: the blockquote says nothing of a 'cattle' search or germinal codes, and the statement follows from commodities search being another ticket's work.

Quote "No visible message is added for an add or remove without JavaScript." is at line 23. The statement is a faithful restatement, and the claim is honest that the blockquote carries no 'without JavaScript' qualifier, pointing at the gap claim for what the qualifier leaves unsettled.

Quote is the setting note at lines 3-4 across the wrap, word for word. The statement's "the owner of the work" is not in the source; it comes from what a ruling source is, and does not change the fact recorded. Holds, with that one word flagged as the extractor's framing.

Gap confirmed: I searched every line of the file. The blockquote says only "a different ticket" (line 8) and Decided item 2 only "a separate ticket" (line 19). No ticket key, tracker or owner appears anywhere in the file, so the source is indeed silent.

Gap confirmed: lines 19-20 say the call stays blocked until that ticket has been implemented and nothing about who reopens it or when it is revisited. The file ends at line 23 with the transit decision.

Gap confirmed: "does not go to the designer before then" (line 20) is the only mention of the designer besides the setting note's "session with the new interaction designer" (lines 3-4). Neither says whether every design route is barred or only that session.

Gap confirmed: the file never mentions adding a country the moment it is picked, removing one without a page load, or 'Added' / 'Removed' announcements. Decided item 3 settles only the visible message, and only without JavaScript. conflicts.json c-006 does hold those three on design question 4, so the note is accurate.

Gap confirmed, and it is the sharpest reading of the file: line 6 says germline in general does not suit the waiting-on-design theme, while Decided item 1 moves only the 'Choose date' calendar (inc-192) out of it. No other germinal row is named anywhere in the file.
